preconditions.description: The first line of stdin is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 30) representing the number of points to be named.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= x <= 10**9 and 0 <= y <= 10**9 for x, y in points)
preconditions.description: All points printed must have integer coordinates within the range [0, 10^9] for both x and y.
Exactly n distinct points must be printed, one per iteration.

preconditions.expression: all(color in ['black', 'white'] for color in colors)
preconditions.description: After each point is printed, the response is either 'black' or 'white'.

postconditions.expression: len(points) == n and len(colors) == n and len(line) == 4
postconditions.description: The program must output exactly n points, receive n colors, and finally output a line defined by two distinct points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2).
The line coordinates (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) must be within the range [0, 10^9].

postconditions.expression: (x1 != x2 or y1 != y2) and (x1 == x2 and y1 == y2) == False
postconditions.description: The two points defining the line must be distinct.

postconditions.expression: all((y2 - y1) * (x - x1) - (x2 - x1) * (y - y1) > 0 if color == 'black' else (y2 - y1) * (x - x1) - (x2 - x1) * (y - y1) < 0 for (x, y), color in zip(points, colors))
postconditions.description: The line must separate all black points from all white points, with no points lying on the line. The sign of the cross product determines the side of the line.
